name: Portugal
sources: GDP $78.7bn and population 9.98m: World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.CD and SP.POP.TOTL, series PRT, 1990 (78,713,860,217 and 9,983,218). Same series as the rest of the roster. Portugal and Greece have almost identical populations and Portuguese output is a fifth smaller; both are a seventh of Spain's, which is the arithmetic of the Iberian peninsula in 1990.

Inflation 13.6%: World Bank FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG, PRT 1990 = 13.631%. The second-highest in Western Europe after Greece. The escudo was on a crawling peg of pre-announced devaluations that was only abandoned in October 1990, and the crawl was itself an inflation machine.

Policy rate 16.9%: three-month Lisbon money-market rate, monthly mean of 1990 = 16.902% (OECD MEI via FRED, IR3TIB01PTM156N). Above Spain's 14.7 on the same peninsula in the same year, and the gap is the credibility difference between a currency inside the ERM band since June 1989 and one that was not admitted until April 1992.

Revenue 27% of GDP: OECD Revenue Statistics, total tax revenue as a share of GDP, Portugal 1990 (about 26.5%). Far below Spain's 0.38, and the gap is real - a large informal sector and a tax administration that was rebuilt only over the following decade.
Gross public debt 60% of GDP: IMF World Economic Outlook GGXWDG_NGDP, PRT 1990 = 60.2%.
Military 1.8% of GDP: World Bank MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS (SIPRI), PRT 1990 = 1.841%. Identical to Spain's 0.018 and on a fifth of the output.

Strength index 8: about 87,000 active personnel, largely conscript, with equipment that was mostly American hand-me-downs - M48 tanks, A-7 Corsairs - and a navy sized for the Atlantic approaches and the Azores rather than for a fleet action. Indexed at half Spain's 16, which is roughly the ratio of the two defence budgets, and above Austria's 6.

Gross fixed capital formation 26.7% of GDP: World Bank NE.GDI.FTOT.ZS, PRT 1990. Split into public 3.9% and private 22.8% using the AMECO general-government series, private as residual - the high public share is the European Community structural and cohesion transfers arriving, which by the mid-1990s ran at 3-4% of Portuguese GDP a year. CAVEAT: total transcribed, public share entered from reference knowledge of AMECO.

Stability 74 and authoritarianism 0.14: just below France's 75 and above Spain's 70. Cavaco Silva's absolute majority of July 1987 was the first single-party majority since the revolution of 1974 and it ended thirteen years in which no Portuguese government had finished a term. Authoritarianism at Spain's 0.13 rounded up by a point: the Council of the Revolution, the military body with a constitutional veto, was abolished only in 1982, and the constitution's commitment to a transition to socialism was removed only in 1989.

Separatism 0.03: at France's 0.03. The Azores and Madeira are autonomous regions with their own governments and their own regionalist parties; Madeira's Alberto Joao Jardim governed it as a personal fief from 1978. Real, formalised, and nowhere near a secession question.

TFP trend 0.014: at France's 0.014 and well above Spain's 0.009, which needs saying because Portugal was much the poorer of the two. That is the reason: Portuguese output per head was around half the Community average in 1990 and the convergence room ahead of it was correspondingly larger. Portugal grew faster than the Community average through the first half of the 1990s and then stopped, which the model can find on its own.

pop_growth_1990 = 0.0175%/yr. Compound annual growth of World Bank SP.POP.TOTL, series PRT (Portugal): 9,996,232 in 1984 to 10,005,000 in 1989 — the five years ending on the eve of the 1 January 1990 start date. See EconomyRecord::pop_growth_1990 in spheres-sim/src/data/mod.rs for why the window ends in 1989 and not with the single-year 1990 rate.

note: 1990 TECHNOLOGY: AUTHORED, NOT DERIVED. What this nation knew on 1 January 1990 is transcribed and sourced grant by grant, exactly like every other 1990 figure in this file, and is not read off tfp_trend - there was never a code path from the trend to the known set, and the zero that stood there was a claim about the world rather than an absence of one (BIBLE section 8 and iron rule 4, both amended 2026-08-30). THE PREDICATE IS SPLIT, and split by the technology's OWN EFFECT TYPE so that it is mechanically computable and never a per-nation judgement call. A node whose effects include MilitaryEfficiency, MilitaryStrength, DiffusionEmission or CostReduction is SOVEREIGNTY-SIDE: holding it means this nation could PRODUCE it, so operating an imported article does not qualify. Every other node is USE-SIDE: deployed and in operational use here is enough, whoever built it, because the effect such a node pays is a productivity, health or output effect and that effect is real in the country where the machine runs. Of the 48 technologies the tree lets anyone hold in 1990, 17 are sovereignty-side and 31 are use-side.

DATA-KEYED TAIL NATION. This nation is outside the 29 authored majors, so nothing here was authored technology by technology: a grant is made only where one of two named published global series supports it, and nothing is modelled, estimated or interpolated. A short list, or an empty one, is the correct outcome of that rule and not a gap in the work.

Data-keyed tail nation: not one of the 29 authored majors. Only the two series named in ruling 3 were consulted - WHO/UNICEF WUENIC DTP3 1990 and World Bank IT.CEL.SETS. Nothing was modelled, estimated or interpolated, and no other evidence was admitted. ISO3 key used for both series: PRT.
WUENIC DTP3 1990 = 89% against the 80% UCI-1990 threshold: bio_universal_immunisation GRANTED.
IT.CEL.SETS at 31 December 1989 = 2782 against a threshold of any positive count: comm_cellular_analogue GRANTED.

The other 46 grantable 1990 technologies are BLANK for this nation by design, not by oversight: the 17 sovereignty-side entries are unreachable by any use-in-operation series, and no published global series was named that keys the remaining 29 use-side entries.

granted.source: World Bank WDI IT.CEL.SETS 'Mobile cellular subscriptions', retrieved from the World Bank indicator API (api.worldbank.org/v2), source id 2, lastupdated 2026-07-13. Series values: PRT, 1989 = 2782 subscriptions and 1990 = 6500 subscriptions. The series is a YEAR-END STOCK, so the 1989 figure describes 31 December 1989, i.e. the game's start instant of 1 January 1990: a network was carrying paying subscribers before the start date. All cellular in service at that date was analogue (NMT, AMPS, TACS, C-Netz, RTMS); GSM had no commercial service anywhere until mid-1991.

WHO/UNICEF WUENIC DTP3 immunisation coverage (% of surviving infants), retrieved from the UNICEF public SDMX API, dataflow UNICEF:IMMUNISATION(1.0), indicator IM_DTP3, DATA_SOURCE field 'WHO/UNICEF estimates of national immunization coverage, 2025 revision'. Series value: PRT, 1990 = 89%, at or above the 80% WHO/UNICEF Universal Childhood Immunization (UCI-1990) target that defines this technology's name.
